title: Gold May Test ₹1.5 Lakh by Diwali, but Experts See Limited Upside
excerpt: Weak momentum, rising bond yields and a stronger dollar cap both metals, says commodity expert Anuj Gupta — while ₹1.5 lakh gold quietly pushes festive buyers toward silver.
body:
• Commodity expert Anuj Gupta expects gold to test ₹1.5 lakh per 10 grams and silver ₹2.2–2.3 lakh per kg by Diwali, but sees limited upside after this year's run.
  • Gold is up about 9% this year while silver is down nearly 9%, Gupta told Business Today, with rising interest rates, inflation and bond yields capping momentum.
  • MCX futures recently traded near ₹1,51,629 per 10 grams for gold and ₹2,29,400 per kg for silver, both down about 1.8–1.9% in early trade.
  • At ₹1.5 lakh per 10 grams, gold is pushing middle-class festive buyers toward silver — the same money buys roughly 650 grams of silver — and jewellers are expanding silver ranges for Diwali.

If you are buying gold this Dhanteras, the expert consensus is: do not expect a bargain, and do not expect a runaway rally either. Commodity expert Anuj Gupta told Business Today that gold could test ₹1.5 lakh per 10 grams and silver ₹2.2 lakh to ₹2.3 lakh per kg by Diwali, but that momentum in both metals is weak, with rising interest rates, sticky inflation and growing interest in bonds pulling money away from bullion. Gold has gained around 9% this year, he noted, while silver has fallen nearly 9%, and industrial demand for silver is also under pressure.

Where prices actually stand

Domestic futures show how close those levels already are. MCX gold recently traded around ₹1,51,629 per 10 grams, down ₹2,831 or about 1.83% in early trade, within a range of roughly ₹1,51,401 to ₹1,54,783. Silver futures traded near ₹2,29,400 per kg, down about 1.9%, according to DW24 News' compilation of MCX data. A stronger dollar and higher US Treasury yields have weighed on both metals, raising the opportunity cost of holding assets that pay no yield.

The silver shift in jewellery stores

The more visible Diwali story may be silver's. With gold at ₹1.5 lakh per 10 grams pricing out a large section of middle-class buyers, the same budget buys about 650 grams of silver at ₹2.3 lakh per kg. Jewellers and traders told the Economic Times, in a report carried by 10BM News, that silver is expected to take a greater share of festive jewellery purchases this season, and retailers are expanding offerings from ornaments and idols to furniture to capture it. Some affluent buyers are going further, betting silver could climb back toward ₹4 lakh per kg.

What buyers should do with this

For diaspora families buying in India this festive season, the practical points are unchanged by the forecasts. Retail prices differ from MCX futures: purity, GST, making charges and the jeweller's premium all sit on top. Confirm the day's 24-carat and 22-carat rates with your jeweller, insist on a bill that separates weight, purity and making charges, and check the live rate immediately before paying — prices are moving by thousands of rupees within single sessions. Gupta's "limited upside" call cuts both ways: it argues against panic-buying at any price before Diwali, and against waiting for a deep correction that forecasters do not see coming.
